title: Tide and Vow
premise: Rafael Whitlock abandoned the concert stage after his hands failed him mid-performance, retreating to a coastal town where he repairs boats and avoids the cello gathering dust in his closet. When a November snowstorm strands him with Isolde Marchetti — the rival soloist who once beat him for every prize that mattered, and the woman he loved and lost a decade ago — the two are forced to share a shuttered seaside inn with the unresolved wreckage of their past. As the storm traps them, old rivalries reignite into honesty, and Rafael must decide whether his identity is his broken career or the man still capable of devotion. They confess everything before the last ferry of the season departs, choosing each other over the versions of themselves they've been hiding behind, and Rafael plays again — not for an audience, but for her, at the dock as spring's first ferry arrives.
about_author: Noor Eriksen is a former orchestral violinist who left touring life to write love stories set in cold, beautiful places. She lives on a windswept peninsula with her partner and a dog named after a concerto.

chapters.title: The Silence After the Applause
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A flashback to his catastrophic final performance — his left hand seizing mid-Elgar before a stunned hall — then cut to the present, where he sands hulls in a boatyard and refuses a friend's invitation to a charity gala. Emotional beat: grief disguised as routine, and the first crack in it when he hears a cello recording in a café.

chapters.title: A Name He Never Forgot
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the gala he attends only to appease his friend, Rafael learns Isolde Marchetti is headlining a winter festival nearby. Ten years of carefully curated avoidance collapses. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing, and the realization he never stopped keeping score.

chapters.title: Snowfall Warning
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde, at the peak of a career that feels increasingly hollow, drives to the coastal town to scout the festival venue and escape her manager's demands. The forecast turns ugly. Emotional beat: exhaustion with her own polished life, and a strange pull toward the town where Rafael grew up.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm closes the coastal road; Isolde's car slides into a ditch and Rafael, the only soul with a tow chain, pulls her out. Both recognize each other in the falling snow. Emotional beat: shock, hostility, and the electric unwanted awareness that neither has changed as much as they claim.

chapters.title: The Last Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The only open lodging is the shuttered Harborlight Inn, whose elderly owner, Maren, takes pity and reopens two rooms — and one shared sitting room, one shared kitchen. Forced proximity begins. Emotional beat: prickly negotiation of space, old wounds surfacing as sarcasm about old competitions.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They draft an uneasy truce: no talk of the past, no talk of the festival, no cello. Rafael discovers Isolde still carries the scar from the night she chose a competition over him. Emotional beat: the truce as a fragile dam, already leaking.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought In
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Power fails; they cook by gaslight and Isolde finds Rafael's childhood photo wall — including one of the two of them at nineteen, inseparable before rivalry poisoned them. Emotional beat: nostalgia ambushing them both, the first honest laugh in a decade.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Their Twenties
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Confined and half-drunk on Maren's plum brandy, they finally speak of the night they almost ran away together — and the night Isolde chose the Tchaikovsky prize instead. The argument turns into a kiss. Emotional beat: ten years of resentment combusting into desire.

chapters.title: Morning, Regretted
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde wakes first, panics, and retreats into career armor: she has a life, a manager, a tour, none of which include him. Rafael finds her rehearsing excuses. Emotional beat: the old pattern reasserting itself — loving in the past tense as self-protection.

chapters.title: Hands
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Isolde finds the dust-sheeted cello in Rafael's room and asks him to play; he refuses, and for the first time names what happened — not stage fright, but a neurological condition he's never told anyone. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the true intimacy, deeper than the kiss.

chapters.title: Maren's Story
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (brief). The innkeeper, widowed young, watches the two guests circle each other and tells Isolde about her own late husband: how she once lent pieces of her heart for years instead of risking the whole thing. Emotional beat: gentle, external wisdom that reframes the lovers' stalemate.

chapters.title: The Rival's Confession
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde admits the truth she's hidden for a decade: she lost the final to Rafael's playing that last season — the judges told her so — and her entire career was built on out-running a ghost. Emotional beat: shame transformed into relief, and a new, dangerous honesty between them.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The storm breaks; the road reopens, and with it the exit both have been pretending not to want. They spend one unguarded day walking the frozen shore, and Rafael lets himself imagine a future. Emotional beat: fragile, sunlit hope that neither dares to voice.

chapters.title: The Manager Arrives
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde's manager arrives with the festival contract — a season that would keep her touring for two years — and Rafael, overhearing the terms, withdraws into courtesy. Emotional beat: the outside world crashing in, loyalty to ambition versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Old Scores
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At a festival reception Rafael must attend, a rival conductor publicly needles him about his ruined hands, and Isolde defends him fiercely — then he pushes her away, ashamed of being seen as damaged. Emotional beat: self-sabotage at the moment of rescue; the lowest ebb.

chapters.title: The Empty Dock
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde finds Rafael at the dock where they once planned to run away, and he tells her he'd rather keep the memory perfect than risk ruining it with a broken man's reality. She walks away. Emotional beat: heartbreak as the price of half-love; both realize lending pieces isn't enough.

chapters.title: What the Cello Knows
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Alone, Rafael opens the case and plays for the first time in years — badly, painfully, then with something like grace. He understands his hands didn't end his music; his fear did. Emotional beat: the turning point, identity reclaimed on his own terms.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The final ferry departs tomorrow; Isolde must sign the contract or walk away from her career's summit. Rafael races to the terminal to stop her — and instead of asking her to stay, he asks her to choose him with her whole heart, offering his own whole and broken self. Emotional beat: climax; the vow, spoken plainly, no pieces.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One Direction
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde tears up the contract's exclusivity clause and negotiates a life that fits — a festival residency here, touring on her terms — and boards the ferry's return crossing with Rafael. Emotional beat: the choice made not by sacrifice but by redesign; belonging chosen, not defaulted.

chapters.title: Winter Festival
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael performs at the festival — a short, imperfect, triumphant cello set, Isolde playing beside him. The town that watched him break watches him begin again. Emotional beat: public redemption, private joy, the past tense finally released.

chapters.title: The Harborlight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Quiet epilogue-adjacent chapter: the two restore the inn's sitting room with Maren, argue happily about repertoire, and Rafael's hands tremble only when Isolde touches them. Emotional beat: domesticity as hard-won reward; loyalty and truth no longer at war.

chapters.title: First Ferry of Spring
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, the first ferry of the season arrives carrying festival guests, and Rafael proposes on the dock where everything was almost lost — Isolde answers before he finishes the question. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; the vow made permanent, the tide finally in their favor.
